My experience at this clinic was quite disappointing.

During my cat's appointment, she received the trivalent vaccine and the Versifel FeLV vaccine. The veterinarian told me that the FeLV vaccine would only need a booster in a year. Later, I consulted the vaccine's technical data sheet and found that, for an unvaccinated cat, the first vaccination consists of two doses with an interval of 3 to 4 weeks. When I returned to the clinic for clarification, the veterinarian had no answer and simply said that "there are several ways to do it" and that, "if I wanted," they could administer another dose. I expected a well-founded explanation based on the manufacturer's recommendations, not a vague answer.

I also had a problem with the billing. On the day of the appointment, the price list included a price for the trivalent vaccine, another for FeLV, and a specific price for administering both vaccines at the same time. However, I was charged separately, paying an additional €13. When I questioned them, they said it was probably a mistake and that they would contact me that day or the next. They never did.

When I returned to the clinic, I found that the price for the combined vaccination had already been removed from the price list. First, they insisted they had called me (which they hadn't), and then they said they had removed that price because that combined vaccine "no longer exists." This doesn't change the fact that this was the advertised price on the day the service was provided. This is called misleading advertising.

What displeased me most was not just the mistake, but the way the whole situation was handled: lack of clarification, contradictory answers, and absence of follow-up. Trust between a pet owner and a veterinary clinic is based on rigor, transparency, and honesty. Unfortunately, that's precisely what I felt was lacking in this experience.
People who truly care about animals, not just wallets; quality service at affordable prices, all done with great care and affection. From now on, this is our go-to veterinarian.

Run away from this veterinarian. You'll be immensely well-received whenever things go well. However, there's enormous incompetence that will always be covered up by the person in charge, who is the owner of this "place." I have three cases in my family where animals died. Recently, my cat died during a sterilization procedure at only 9 months old, even after pre-surgery exams that returned results in accordance with the procedure. A STERILIZATION! MY FRIENDS! Where I was told it was an allergy to the anesthesia, something that happens with a 1% probability. Believe me, I didn't pursue legal action against this establishment because the pain was immense, and nothing would bring our pet back. And it would have been a process I didn't want to subject my animal to. Saving our energy to heal from the pain they certainly caused us through negligence. I hope they have the greatest failure in this business and that my criticism makes people think twice before leaving their companions "here." Furthermore, I should add that any impolite or insensitive comment regarding this criticism will prompt me to take the necessary steps to respond in a different way. Please be aware.
